newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Porst stake cost 90.4 mln Sfr - Spector.
newsitem.headline: Porst stake cost 90.4 mln Sfr - Spector.

text.p: Belgian photoprocessing group Spector Photo Group NV said on Friday its parent company Fotoinvest would pay 90.4 million Swiss francs for its 58.1 percent stake of Switzerland's Porst.
"This means that the value of Porst Holding as a whole is being estimated at 155 million Swiss francs," Spector said in a statement.

Spector said last month it signed a definitive agreement with the former Interdiscount Holding Ag, now named Distefora, to acquire a majority stake in Porst -- a Swiss photogroup with operations in Germany and Hungary.

Spector said it would pay 25.15 million Swiss francs of the purchase price in cash. The rest would be paid for through the takeover of the debts that Distefora has against Porst Holding (55.86 million Swiss francs), and ASCO Ag (9.38 million Swiss francs).

It added that doubts whether Distefora could pay back its debts to Porst Holding and the bad performance of Distefora in general on the Swiss stock market explained the current low price of the Porst share.

Spector also that for the 100 percent of Interdiscount France it had agreed to buy it would pay one French franc but with the obligation to supply an additional financing of 120 million French francs in the form of a subordinated loan.

Distefora will, before the sale of Interdiscount France, raise the equity of Interdiscount France by 467 million French francs, of which 160 million in cash and 307 million through the conversion of shareholders loans.
The resulting balance sheet would show a net own equity 350 million French francs.
